feature_contracts.description: After reset the design shall present a deterministic safe idle state with no valid actuator update and fault reporting asserted until software clears it.
A firmware write to the control register shall be accepted through the MMIO interface and reflected in the CSR read data path.
The request packer shall drive request valid/data outputs and keep the request packet stable while the external requester is not ready.
The response unpacker shall consume response valid/data inputs and drive response ready as an output.
A faulted or malformed response path shall inhibit actuator validity and assert safe mode.

When an authorized response is accepted, the actuator command shall be clamped to the programmed bounds and remain within the strict scenario-derived subrange that represents a safe bounded command window.
A firmware fault-clear write shall be decoded through the CSR path and influence the latched fault state under top-level supervision.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level integration point that owns the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface, request packer, response unpacker, safety supervisor, and optional bounded history capture. All externally visible outputs are driven by real RTL logic.
top_module.functionality: Implements the top-level firmware control-plane, request transport, response transport, response decode, safety supervision, and actuator command authorization. It provides deterministic reset behavior, explicit transport directionality, and bounded actuator command behavior without implementing the surrogate network or any physics compute.
responsibilities: Expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and response/ready semantics.
Pack compact 128-bit external-model requests from configuration, flow metadata, geometry-handle metadata, sequence, and timestamp.
Unpack compact 128-bit response packets into recommendation, status, sequence echo, timestamp echo, and validity fields.
Authorize actuator updates only when enable, handshake completion, response validity, sequence match, freshness, and fault-free conditions are all satisfied.
Clamp accepted actuator commands between programmed min/max bounds and apply rate limiting when configured.
Inhibit actuator validity and assert safe-mode/fault reporting on invalid, stale, timeout, malformed, or replayed packets.
top_module.reset_behavior: On reset, the CSR interface returns deterministic defaults, request valid is deasserted, response ready is driven to its idle value, actuator validity is deasserted, actuator fault is asserted or held latched for software handling, and safe mode is asserted. No fallback command substitution occurs.
behavior_rules: req_valid and req_data are outputs; req_ready is an input. rsp_valid and rsp_data are inputs; rsp_ready is an output.
A model request may only be considered launched when req_valid and req_ready are asserted together.
A model response may only be considered accepted when rsp_valid and rsp_ready are asserted together.
No raw geometry or tensor payloads may appear at the top level; only compact handles and metadata are permitted.
No GPU-specific compute and no surrogate neural-network inference may be implemented in RTL.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
modules.description: CSR/MMIO register block that implements firmware-visible control and status registers and provides decoded semantic fields to the request packer and safety supervisor.
modules.functionality: Implements the full firmware-visible register window. Registers include enable, mode select, safe-position command, min/max bounds, rate-limit setting, timeout threshold, stale-data threshold, sequence counters, geometry handle, flow metadata, last-seen timestamp, fault clear, fault status, and link-health indicators. All declared registers are reachable through decode and software-visible through the MMIO interface.
responsibilities: Decode all documented MMIO addresses.
Latch writable configuration fields.
Return read data and ready/accept semantics.
Expose firmware-visible status and fault indicators.
Provide a fault-clear strobe to software control logic.
modules.reset_behavior: Writable configuration registers reset to deterministic defaults: enable low, mode select zero, safe position set to a defined safe code, min/max bounds to safe defaults, rate limit zero or disabled, timeout and stale thresholds to conservative defaults, sequence counters reset, geometry handle and flow metadata reset, and fault-clear deasserted. Readback returns these defaults until software writes new values.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
No internal state may be mislabeled as software-visible unless it is decoded here.
This block is the sole producer of semantic configuration fields used by other modules.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_req_packer
modules.description: Composes the 128-bit outbound request packet from semantic configuration, flow metadata, geometry handle, sequence number, timestamp, and link-health metadata.
modules.functionality: Builds the outbound external-model request packet and drives the request-channel valid/data outputs. The packet carries only compact metadata, sequence, timestamp, and link-health information; it never carries raw geometry or large tensor payloads.
responsibilities: Assemble 128-bit request payload fields.
Emit req_valid and req_data as outputs per the transport direction contract.
Provide launched sequence and timestamp information to downstream logic.
Use geometry handle or ID only, never raw geometry.
Maintain stable request data while valid is asserted and ready is low.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, request outputs are cleared and no packet launch occurs. Sequence and timestamp outputs are reset to known values until configuration becomes valid.
behavior_rules: req_valid is asserted only when the request packet is well-formed and the control plane permits transmission.
The packet must remain stable while req_valid is high and req_ready is low.
No surrogate model computation is performed here.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_rsp_unpacker
modules.description: Decodes the 128-bit external response packet into command recommendation, status flags, validity bits, sequence echo, timestamp echo, and malformed indicators.
modules.functionality: Unpacks the external response packet and reports response acceptance metadata to the safety supervisor. It does not compute aerodynamics or emulate the surrogate service.
responsibilities: Decode response payload fields.
Provide response validity and malformed indications.
Capture sequence echo and timestamp echo for the safety supervisor.
Drive rsp_ready as the output-side ready signal per the transport contract.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, response-derived outputs are cleared and rsp_ready is driven to a quiescent idle value until the top-level can accept traffic.
behavior_rules: Response decode must be synchronous and registered for timing closure.
Malformed encodings or invalid validity bits must be reported to the safety supervisor.
The decoder never substitutes or transforms the recommended command into a fallback command; it only reports what was received.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety_supervisor
modules.description: Sequence, timeout, stale-data, fault, and authorization supervisor that decides whether actuator updates may be applied. It gates valid updates only when enable, handshake completion, response validity, sequence echo, freshness, and fault conditions all satisfy the contract.
modules.functionality: Evaluates authorization for actuator updates. It checks global enable, request/response handshake completion, response validity, sequence echo match, response age against timeout, stale-data threshold, sequence gaps/replays, malformed packets, and fault bits. It clamps and rate-limits the candidate command only when authorized. Otherwise it inhibits valid updates and asserts fault reporting and safe mode without silently substituting a different command.
responsibilities: Authorize or inhibit actuator updates based on the full safety contract.
Enforce min/max clamp and programmable rate limiting on accepted command recommendations.
Detect timeout, stale-data, sequence mismatch, replay, and malformed response conditions.
Latch fault status for software handling.
Drive link-health indicators for firmware visibility.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, actuator_valid is deasserted, actuator_fault is asserted or held latched until software clear, safe_mode is asserted, and supervisory error flags are cleared to known states. The module does not emit a fallback substitute command; it simply inhibits validity when not authorized.
behavior_rules: Authorized actuator updates require enable, completed request/response handshake, valid response, matching sequence echo, freshness within timeout/stale thresholds, and no fault bits.
Sequence gaps, replays, or echo mismatches assert seq_error and prevent valid updates.
Timeout or stale-data expiry asserts safe_mode and inhibits actuator_valid.
Rate limiting is applied only to accepted updates and only within the programmed delta per update.
No silent command replacement is allowed on invalid or faulted conditions.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_history_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral memory wrapper for compact request/response history or debug capture. It is intended to map to native block RAM in FPGA implementation and must not be flattened into registers.
modules.functionality: Provides a small bounded history store for recent compact packets or state snapshots. The wrapper exists only as a technology-neutral memory abstraction and must be inferred or mapped to block RAM through the specified memory macro contract.
responsibilities: Expose a simple synchronous RAM-style interface.
Support compact history capture without large register flattening.
Deliver readback data to the top-level supervisor or debug logic.
modules.reset_behavior: Memory output is quiescent after reset; stored contents may be undefined unless explicitly written, but the interface behavior remains synchronous and synthesizable.
behavior_rules: This module is a wrapper only; the authoritative implementation contract is the memory macro named in memory_macros.
No alternate behavioral memory model identity may be created in RTL.
The memory dout must be consumed by real RTL logic or exposed through a top-level output; it may not be left dangling.
